Clinical details:
Lateral T wave inversion on ECG. Echo: septal thickness 18 mm. Father died suddenly aged 52. ?Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

Technique:
Cardiac MRI at 1.5 T. Cine SSFP imaging in standard long- and short-axis planes, T2-weighted STIR, native T1 and T2 mapping, post-contrast T1 mapping and late gadolinium enhancement imaging following 0.1 mmol/kg gadobutrol.

Findings:
The left ventricle is normal in size with asymmetric septal hypertrophy, maximal end-diastolic wall thickness 19 mm in the basal anteroseptum (basal inferolateral wall 9 mm). Systolic function is hyperdynamic with no regional wall motion abnormality. LVEDVi 72 ml/m², LVESVi 20 ml/m², LVEF 72%, LV mass index 98 g/m². No systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve and no flow acceleration in the left ventricular outflow tract at rest.

The right ventricle is normal in size with preserved systolic function. RVEDVi 74 ml/m², RVESVi 30 ml/m², RVEF 59%.

The left atrium is mildly dilated. No significant valvular regurgitation or stenosis.

No pericardial effusion. No significant extracardiac findings.

Tissue characterisation:
Native T1 1068 ms (local reference range 950–1050 ms at 1.5 T). T2 49 ms (local reference range 42–52 ms). ECV 31% (normal <30%). No myocardial oedema. Raised native T1 and ECV indicate diffuse interstitial expansion.

Late gadolinium enhancement:
Patchy mid-wall enhancement at the anterior and inferior right ventricular insertion points and within the hypertrophied basal anteroseptum, approximately 4% of LV mass. No subendocardial enhancement to suggest prior infarction. The pattern of enhancement is not suggestive of cardiac amyloidosis or Anderson–Fabry disease. No intracardiac thrombus.

Conclusion:
1. Asymmetric septal hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, maximal wall thickness 19 mm, without resting left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.
2. Patchy mid-wall fibrosis (approximately 4% of LV mass) with raised ECV.
3. Hyperdynamic left ventricular systolic function (LVEF 72%).
4. Suggest referral to the inherited cardiac conditions service; first-degree relatives should be offered screening.
